- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.4) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days to counteract mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 3–7% downward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values or apply 1–3% dampening factor.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after 15–20 days (e.g., >10% drop from peak), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; apply 2–5% upward bias for next 5–10 days to offset underestimation.
